reforms.description: The Administration proposed to extend the Research and Experimentation tax credit, which was scheduled to expire at the end of fiscal 1995, at a cost of $17 billion over five years and subject to pay-as-you-go budget rules.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the effective cost of private R&D investment, incentivizing firms to increase innovation spending and productivity-enhancing research.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'proposed to extend', indicating announcement but not yet legislated or implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant extension of an existing major tax instrument with substantial fiscal cost ($17 billion over five years), but not a structural system-wide change.
reforms.source_quote: First, a number of tax provisions are scheduled to expire before the end of the budget planning horizon in 1999 (most prominently the Research and Experimentation tax credit at the end of fiscal 1995)... The total cost involved would be $17 billion over the next five years.

reforms.description: The National Competitiveness Act provides $1.9 billion for closer government-industry ties, including a $100 million venture capital provision for joint ventures and nearly $600 million for flat-panel display technology development.
reforms.component_name: Venture capital and flat-panel display technology support
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Combines venture capital support for joint ventures and sectoral technology development, both of which enhance innovation capacity, firm formation, and productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text indicates the Act 'provides' funding, but no explicit evidence of legislative passage or implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Comprehensive legislative package with $1.9 billion in funding across multiple innovation support mechanisms (venture capital, government-industry collaboration, sectoral R&D), representing a significant structural initiative.
reforms.source_quote: A so-called National Competitiveness Act is also being debated in the Congress. Its latest version provides $1.9 billion for forging closer ties between the government and industry. A venture capital provision provides $100 million for government participation of up to five years duration in joint ventures where the grant recipients pay at least half of all costs. Nearly $600 million of the total would go to flat-panel displays, a test case for the new, more activist technology policy.

reforms.description: Two sectoral R&D initiatives supporting advanced technology development: NASA awarded a $1.5 billion research contract for High Speed Civil Transport (supersonic aircraft) development, and the Defense Department announced a plan to spend $587 million over five years (eventually $1 billion total) to support development of a domestic flat-panel display screen industry to compete with Japanese producers.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Both initiatives target strategic sectors (aerospace, semiconductors/displays) where domestic capability and competitiveness are critical for long-term productivity and technological leadership.
reforms.status_evidence: Index 4 explicitly states 'announced a plan'; index 2 states 'awarded', suggesting implementation has begun, but both are announced in 1994.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D commitments with substantial funding ($1.5 billion and $1 billion respectively), but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms; focused on specific technology domains.
reforms.source_quote: The Defense Department announces a plan to spend $587 million over the next five years (and eventually a total of $1 billion) to support the development of a domestic industry to produce flat-panel display screens.

reforms.description: The United States agreed to extend patent terms to 20 years from the date of application (compared with 17 years from the date of grant), ease patent protest procedures, and make patent applications open for public inspection 18 months after submission.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Extended patent terms strengthen intellectual property protection, incentivizing private R&D investment and commercialization; streamlined procedures reduce transaction costs for innovators.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'agreed to', indicating announcement of policy agreement but no explicit evidence of legislative passage or implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reform of the patent system affecting the incentive structure for innovation and commercialization, but not a structural overhaul of the innovation system.
reforms.source_quote: Over the summer an agreement was reached in the area of patents: for its part the United States agreed to extend patent terms to 20 years from the date of application as compared with 17 years from the date of grant; to ease the process of protesting the granting of a patent; and to make patent applications open for public inspection 18 months after submission.
